Four verification states is already near the limit of what a twenty-second scan can absorb. If a fifth is ever added, the badge stops being scannable and becomes a legend the reader has to learn.

/lab is the section most likely to be dead weight. It is defensible only while the token set is genuinely growing; if the design settles and the lab is not updated, it becomes a page showing five boxes.

Shipping the router without public/404.html and the main.tsx restore block in the same commit silently breaks every deep link on Pages, and it breaks in a way local dev will never reveal. This is the one ordering mistake that costs the most.

The portfolio has no logic layer today and the vite config says so honestly. Adding the router makes that comment false; if the src/router/** coverage gate is not wired at the same time, the page will claim CI discipline it is no longer fully exercising.

The evidence-first fold assumes the reader values verifiability. A recruiter screening for keywords rather than substance may bounce off three numbers where a skills list would have caught them. This design accepts that reader loss.

designs.thesis: That the scarcest thing on an engineering portfolio is a claim you can check, so the page leads with three verified numbers and labels every project with its true evidence level — including the one that has to say PROVISIONAL.

visualDirection.color: Keep the existing palette and add exactly three roles. --color-warning: #b45309 (ported back from climx's tokens.css, which the portfolio dropped — it now has a real consumer in Phynned's PROVISIONAL badge). --color-verified: #15803d (new, for LIVE and ON SILICON). --color-accent-soft: #eef3fd (badge and chip backgrounds). Accent #2255cc stays and is used for exactly three things: links, the ProofStrip numbers on hover, and the card-title hover from EstadoCard.module.css. No decorative fills, no gradients, no colored section backgrounds. Dark mode is net-new — a single @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block redefining only the color roles: bg #0f1115, surface #171a21, text #e8eaed, text-muted #a0a6b0, accent #6c9cf5, border #2a2f3a, warning #d99a4e, verified #5fbb7a; reset.css's `color-scheme: light` becomes `light dark`. No toggle UI — the system preference is the whole mechanism, which keeps the page at zero UI state.
visualDirection.density: High and deliberately front-loaded. Target: header, ProofStrip, positioning line, and all five project cards visible without scrolling at 1440x900. Every card is 6 lines: tag + badge, title, description, evidence, links. Prose is capped at 60ch via a --measure token; the project grid is not, because cards are scanned, not read. Below the fold density relaxes: SkillsTable at gap 3, footer at gap 2. On a project page the MetricList is the densest block on the site and that is correct — it is a table of evidence.
visualDirection.layout: One centered column, .page max-width raised from 44rem to climx's 64rem (the 44rem column cannot hold a three-chip strip or an 18rem auto-fill grid). ProofStrip is a Cluster of three Boxes that wraps to one column on narrow screens with no media query. Projects are Grid min="18rem" gap={4} — auto-fill, so two columns at 64rem and one on a phone, again with no breakpoint. The only media query on the whole site remains the 560px rule already in SkillsTable.module.css. Vertical rhythm is Stack gap={7} between top-level sections and gap={3} inside them, matching the current app.tsx.
visualDirection.motion: Effectively none. No entrance animation, no scroll-triggered anything, no transforms, no parallax. The single transition on the site is 120ms on `color` for card titles and ProofStrip numbers under hover/focus-visible, and it is wrapped in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { transition: none }. Focus outlines are the restored 2px solid var(--color-accent) with 2px offset from climx's reset, applied to both a and button.
visualDirection.typography: system-ui for prose (unchanged from reset.css); --font-mono for every label, tag, badge, metric value and instrument string — the mono/prose split is what makes evidence visually separable from claims at a glance. Add --font-size-700: 2.441rem (continuing the existing 1.25 ratio from 1.953rem) for the name, which at the current 600 max is too small to anchor a fold. All metric values get font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so a column of numbers aligns. Below the fold no heading exceeds size 400. Section headings stay as they are today: size 200, mono, muted, uppercase — a label, not a title.

designs.whatItRefuses: It refuses decoration that carries no information — and specifically, it refuses climx's 32 state photographs. They are unattributed re-encodes of a 2023 school project with no author, license, or source recorded anywhere in that repo (climx's own CreditsPage credits every municipality photo and says of the state photos only that they came from the original project), they are 640x360 and will soften as any hero, and they are photographs of Mexican geography rather than of anything the operator built. A mangrove above a card about pinning threads to V-Cache cores is the visual grammar of a bought template. It also refuses: a hero image or any placeholder art in the three project pages that have no real figure (visible emptiness over borrowed pixels); a profile photograph, which does not exist and is not needed; skill percentage bars or star ratings, which invent precision the CV does not have; the profile paragraph above the fold, because prose loses a twenty-second scan to three numbers; a contact form, because there is no backend and climx's entire stance is that there does not need to be; a dark-mode toggle, because prefers-color-scheme does the job with zero state; any scroll or entrance animation; ErrorState and the whole src/lib data layer, because a page that imports its content at build time has no fetch that can fail and adding them would be exactly the speculative wrapper the house rules forbid; and it refuses to print Phynned's +98% as a benchmark — that project's own README states its numbers must not be cited as validated, so the page shows the direction under a PROVISIONAL badge or not at all.

visualDirection.density: Dense vertically, generous horizontally. Text never exceeds --measure 34rem regardless of viewport. Section rhythm: var(--space-6) between sections, var(--space-5) between project entries, var(--space-3) between HangingRows rows. Hairline --color-border rules appear in exactly three places — under the masthead, between project entries, above the footer. Nowhere else. No borders around anything, no border-radius above 0, no box-shadow, no background fills outside the colophon specimen.
visualDirection.layout: One centred column, .page max-width 45rem (up from 44rem, to fit gutter + gap + measure exactly). Above 52rem — the single media query this design introduces, licensed by tokens.css's own comment that the breakpoint literal is the sanctioned repetition — labelled rows use a hanging gutter: `grid-template-columns: var(--gutter) minmax(0, var(--measure))`, terms right-aligned in mono in the 9rem gutter, prose in the measure column. Below 52rem it collapses to stacked term-above-detail. The project list is a Stack, not a Grid — Grid keeps exactly one consumer, the colophon's spacing specimen.
visualDirection.motion: Effectively none. One 120ms color transition on link hover, wrapped in a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` guard that removes it. No scroll animation, no fade-in, no parallax, no view transitions. climx has no motion rules at all, so this is net-new and deliberately kept to a single property.
visualDirection.typography: Serif body, mono metadata, no sans anywhere. --font-serif: ui-serif, Charter, 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif — system stacks only, nothing fetched, consistent with climx's two-runtime-dependency stance. The existing --font-mono carries every label, status line, link row and measured NUMBER; that last one is a hard rule, because Georgia ships old-style figures that will not align in a measured-values column. Type scale retuned to ~1.2 anchored on a 17px body: 0.8125 / 0.9375 / 1.0625 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 2rem. Leading 1.6 body, 1.25 headings. The name renders at --font-size-500 (1.5rem) — the largest thing on the site is the operator's name, and it is 24px.

designs.whatItRefuses: "It refuses the card grid. The current <Grid min=\"16rem\"> of surface-and-border ProjectCards is deleted, not restyled — five projects laid out as tiles is the visual grammar of a template, and it caps every project at whatever fits in a box. It refuses climx's 32 state photographs, for both of the reasons already on the record: no author or licence is recorded for a single one of them, and they are pictures of Mexican geography, not of the operator's work. It refuses stock photography, generated illustration, project logos, and any decorative image whatsoever — the only images allowed anywhere on this site are artifacts the operator produced, of which exactly two exist on disk today. It refuses a /lab route: a styleguide page for five primitives is a route about the site instead of about the work, so the type specimen goes inside /colophon and earns no URL of its own. It refuses a separate /about page — the profile, work and education are eight lines and belong on the index. It refuses the <details>/<summary> disclosure pattern from CreditsPage: hiding three documentation links behind a summary is furniture, and this page shows its links. It refuses a skills bar chart, a percentage, a star rating, or any other invented quantification of proficiency; skills are a labelled list because that is what the CV honestly contains. It refuses a blog, a writing section, and a 'latest posts' block, because nothing has been written. It refuses badges, counters, GitHub stat cards, analytics, cookie banners and third-party fonts — the colophon says so out loud. And it refuses to print any number without its instrument and date beside it, which means Phynned's headline benchmarks either carry their own project's provisional-and-under-re-validation caveat in the same sentence or do not appear at all."

The router is climx's own declared 'highest execution risk'. The port removes most of that risk (the code is written, tested, and has already had its FATAL found in production and fixed), but one specific failure is silent: if public/404.html's base string and vite.config.ts's base ever disagree, deep links break with no error anywhere. The TOUCHPOINT comment is the only guard, and it is a comment.

This design's cost is concentrated in prose, not code. The five what/how/scope arrays are roughly 60 short paragraphs that only the operator can validate. A half-written content.ts produces five thin detail pages, which is strictly worse than the single good page that exists today. The router should not land until the content does.

ThemeToggle is the weakest item under this lens and I want that on the record. It is 25 tested lines with a real user, and it makes the token system legible — but it is also the one component here that a reader could fairly call a feature added because it was fun. If something has to be cut, cut it first, and cut /lab with it.

MeasuredTable creates an incentive to fill it. The type requires an instrument and a date, which stops the laziest overclaim, but nothing stops someone typing a plausible instrument next to a remembered number. The discipline is social, not mechanical, and it degrades the moment one row is written from memory.

collect-buildinfo.mjs can become a maintenance toy. It has one consumer and it touches git and the test reporter, both of which change shape over time. Its 'unknown' fallback keeps it from breaking the build, but a stamp that quietly reads 'unknown / unknown' for six months is worse than no stamp — it is the page failing its own claim in public.

Four routes and a colophon on a five-project portfolio is close to the ceiling of what the content supports. If the project detail pages turn out thin, the honest correction is to collapse /projects/:slug back into expandable sections on home (climx's CreditsPage native <details> pattern is the ready-made mechanism) and keep only the router-plus-shim work that /engineering already justifies.

designs.thesis: Bet everything on verifiable specifics: port climx's router, deep-link shim and a11y block so the page becomes four real routes, then fill those routes with numbers that carry their instrument and date and with limitations quoted from each project's own README — so the page's credibility comes from what a reader can check, not from what it looks like.

visualDirection.color: The existing palette kept — #ffffff bg, #fafafa surface, #111111 text, #5b5b5b muted, #2255cc accent, #e4e4e4 border — plus --color-accent-weak #e8eefc and --color-warning #8a5a00 / --color-warning-weak #fdf3e0 for StatusChip, which is the first real consumer the warning role has had. Net-new: a dark palette (#0f1115 bg, #161a21 surface, #e8eaed text, #9aa3af muted, #7aa2f7 accent, #262b34 border), defined only as token overrides in two blocks — prefers-color-scheme guarded with :root:not([data-theme='light']), and :root[data-theme='dark'] for the toggle. Every pairing above clears 7:1 on text and 4.5:1 on accents. Color is never the only carrier of meaning: StatusChip prints its status as words.
visualDirection.density: Comfortable for prose, tight for data. Prose blocks are capped at --measure (66ch) even though .page is 60rem, so the reading column never widens past comfort while a table or a diagram can use the full width. Section rhythm is --space-7 (48px) between top-level sections and --space-3 (12px) inside a card — the same steps the existing SkillsTable rows already use. Cards are equal-height by Grid row (height:100% from climx's EstadoCard .link) so a two-line description and a four-line one do not produce a ragged grid.
visualDirection.layout: One centered column, .page max-width 60rem (up from 44rem, because project pages hold a four-column table and a wide diagram). Every layout on all four routes is Stack / Cluster / Grid / Box / Text plus exactly two page-level rules — .page and .prose. No sixth primitive is added; that constraint is the /lab page's actual claim, and breaking it silently would make /lab a lie. Responsiveness comes from Grid's auto-fill minmax and rem type, exactly as climx does it; the single media query in the codebase stays SkillsTable's 560px collapse, joined by the tokens.css dark block.
visualDirection.motion: None. No scroll reveals, no parallax, no entrance animations, no skeleton shimmer. The only transitions are the 120ms color change on link hover and focus. Because there is nothing to reduce, no prefers-reduced-motion rule is needed — which is the honest version of respecting it, rather than a rule that exists to be pointed at.
visualDirection.typography: system-ui for prose, --font-mono for everything that is an instrument reading. That is a rule with a hard edge: project tags, status chips, route paths, filenames, measured values, instruments, dates, the commit sha and the nav wordmark are mono; sentences never are. The type scale gains --font-size-700 (2.441rem, continuing the existing 1.25 ratio) for page h1s and otherwise stays the ported six steps. Headings choose their level semantically and their size separately — the Text primitive already enforces that split by keeping `as` and `size` independent.

designs.whatItRefuses: "It refuses climx's 32 state photographs, on both available grounds: nothing in that repo records an author, licence or source for a single one (climx credits every municipality photo and says of these only that they came from the 2023 project — that contrast is the tell), and they are pictures of Mexican geography, not of Phyriager, PhyriadFG, Phynned, PHarvard, climx or the operator. A mangrove above a card about core pinning is template grammar, and a reader spots it in a second. It refuses every other form of decoration that would imply engineering it does not contain: no hero image, no gradient, no drop shadow, no scroll animation, no icon set, no web font, no analytics. It refuses a separate /about route, because the material — one paragraph, one freelance entry, one education line, three languages — fits on home and a padded page reads as padding. It refuses placeholder Measured sections: a project with no instrumented number shows nothing, never 'coming soon', which is why the Phyriager and PhyriadFG pages will look emptier than the climx one. It refuses to print a bundle size in BuildStamp, because that number is unknowable before the build it would describe and a committed stale one is exactly the fake evidence this page exists to argue against. It refuses to reprint climx's live Lighthouse scores without their caveat, since they were measured at the pre-rename URL. It refuses to port src/lib/data, src/lib/geo, SearchCombobox and ErrorState however good that code is — a page that imports its content at build time has no cache, no staleness, no network failure mode and nothing to search, and shipping them would be cargo-culting the donor. It refuses a sharp devDependency to convert three images once. And it refuses react-router, a CSS framework, and a component library, because the site's entire argument is that this much was built and gated by hand."

strengths: The load-bearing entry is real reuse, verified byte-for-byte. F:\Phyriad\projects\climx\src\router\router.tsx (3,868 B) exports exactly Router/Link/useParams/navigate plus matchPath/stripBase for tests, and computes `const BASE = import.meta.env.BASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '')`. The portfolio's vite.config.ts sets `base: '/portfolio/'`, so the copy works unchanged, as claimed. `fallback` is a REQUIRED prop on Router (`{ routes: Route[]; fallback: ComponentType }`), which independently justifies porting NotFound.tsx. Without this file there is no /projects/:slug and the whole design collapses into the single page that already exists. This is climx doing structural work, not being namedropped.

The 404-shim entry is correct, complete, and correctly ordered. I confirmed climx\public\404.html contains `var base = '/climx/';` with the `~and~` encoding, and that the matching 8-line restore block sits above createRoot in climx\src\main.tsx. I also confirmed `ls F:\Phyriad\projects\portfolio\public` fails (no public/ dir) and that portfolio\src\main.tsx has no restore block. The design's insistence that these ship in the same commit as the router is the single most useful operational statement in the document.

The reset.css diff was done first-hand and every claim checks out. Diffing the two files: the portfolio dropped `input,button,textarea,select { font: inherit }`, the whole `button { ... }` base rule, `button:focus-visible` (it kept only `a:focus-visible`), `.skip-link`, `.skip-link:focus`, and `.page`'s `display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap: var(--space-6)`. climx's `.page` is `max-width: 64rem`, the portfolio's is `44rem`. Five blocks plus the width: all six claims true. The skip-link is genuinely required by the new app shell and 64rem is genuinely required by an 18rem auto-fill grid, so this is structural, not tidying.

MEASUREMENTS.md is the best call in the document and every number survives checking. F:\Phyriad\projects\climx\docs\planning\MEASUREMENTS.md really is a Date | Stage | Metric | Measured | Instrument | Cap table, and I verified in it: 9,852 records to 2,463 files, all-lite.json 44,266 B gzip, 51/51 tests, lib coverage 98.92%, bundle 66.66 KB gzip against the 150 KB M4 cap, state images 123 MB to 1.12 MB, photo coverage 1,474/2,463 (59.8%), Lighthouse 90/100 home and 100/98 municipio, and the self-inflicted 404 (989 of 2,463 municipios had no sidecar). The design's own contentGap that those Lighthouse numbers were taken against swately.github.io/project-tw/ is also true — the header of that section says exactly that.

The refusals are disciplined and mostly correct, which is itself evidence the author read the repo rather than skimmed it. Refusing src\lib\** , SearchCombobox, ForecastCard, skyIcon, CommonsGallery, NearestMunicipio, ErrorState and scripts\*.mjs on the grounds that a build-time content.ts import has no fetch that can fail is the right call and matches the container's no-speculative-layers rule. The estados-photo refusal is factually grounded too: climx\src\pages\CreditsPage.tsx credits every municipality photo but says only that the state photos "provienen del proyecto original (2023)" — no author, no license, exactly as the design states.

No assets are invented. I confirmed on disk: PhyriadFG\docs\diagrams\phyriadfg_multigpu.png = 89,350 B, phyriadfg_pipeline.png = 64,286 B, Phyriager\screenshots\trazado_1.png = 167,722 B, documentos_varios\cv.pdf = 172,883 B. Every byte count in the design matches. The claim that climx has no favicon to inherit is also true — climx\public\ holds only 404.html, data/ and img/.

The primitives claim is honest rather than padded. Diffing all seven files: Box.tsx, Box.module.css, Stack.tsx, Cluster.tsx, Grid.tsx and primitives.test.tsx are byte-identical between the two repos; Text.module.css differs only by the four-line `.mono` block. Reconcile the PHarvard ProofStrip number before it is printed in the largest type on the page. PHarvard\syn\VENDOR_VS_ESTIMATE.md describes the same 2026-08-01 post-bring-up configuration — same 625 registers, same 12 of 26 block RAMs — as "1,402 LUT4 (20 %) ... post-route Fmax 21.744 MHz". Extend the Text primitive's type unions, or the design does not compile. portfolio\src\primitives\Text.tsx declares `size?: 100 | 200 | 300 | 400 | 500 | 600` and `as?: 'p' | 'span' | 'strong' | 'small' | 'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3' | 'dt' | 'dd'`. The design specifies `Text as=h1 size=700` for the name and adds `--font-size-700` to tokens.css, but adding the token is not enough — the union needs `| 700`. Separately, MetricList as a `<dl>` has no primitive that renders one: neither Stack's nor Box's `as` union includes 'dl'. Both are small edits, but the design's claim that "no new layout mechanism is introduced anywhere" quietly implies primitive edits it does not name.

Reconsider the 'no last-updated mechanism' content gap against climx\src\lib\data\staleness.ts. The design declares "there is no mechanism to derive one" while refusing the entire src/lib layer wholesale. Refusing fetchWithCache/useFetch/hooks is correct — there is no fetch. But staleness.ts is twenty JSX-free, zero-dependency lines (`ageHours`, `isStale`, `ageLabel`) that turn one timestamp into a human label, and it is exactly the mechanism the gap says does not exist. Either port the label half over a build-time constant, or state that you saw it and rejected it — do not declare the problem unsolvable while the solution sits in the donor repo.
